..
As of 220 AM Friday...

KEY MESSAGE 1... Typical late-summer weather expected, with isolated 
to scattered late-day showers and storms most days through next 
week. Convection will be focused over the NW (Triad) and far SE 
portions of central NC through this weekend. 

We can't identify with confidence an entirely dry day across all of 
central NC over the next 7 days, as we maintain moist low levels 
within a fairly stagnant large scale pattern, particularly from now 
through the weekend. But, overall, our shower/storm coverage is 
expected to be near or below climatology into the middle of next 
week. Our current mid level pattern consists of a weak trough to our 
W sandwiched between strong anticyclones over the Desert Southwest 
and off the Mid Atlantic coast, while a large Canadian gyre spins 
over N Manitoba, N Ontario, and Hudson Bay, and its associated broad 
trough covers the Upper Midwest and N/W Great Lakes. Anticyclonic 
surface winds from the SSW and SW over NC will persist into Sat, 
around high pressure centered off the Carolina coast and extending 
westward into the Southeast/Carolinas, as a lee trough holds over 
the W Piedmont. Over the next few days, the better convection 
chances over central NC will be in the far SE, associated with the 
inland-tracking sea breeze, and in the NW, where mid level lapse 
rates will be slightly more favorable compared to E NC and where 
mountain storms may drift late in the day. For today/tonight, we're 
likely to be within a PW minimum, with values near or a bit under 
normal, and this combined with a lack of large scale forcing for 
ascent should greatly limit coverage today. We're still expected 
SBCAPE to peak up to 1500-2500 J/kg today, but with very poor deep 
layer bulk shear. Isolated storms are still expected today, likely 
starting on old weak outflows or differential heating zones or on 
the sea breeze, with these isolated storms then translating further 
N and NW through the afternoon and evening. This precip pattern 
should hold through the weekend, albeit with slightly better 
coverage as PW rebounds back above normal (and we can see this batch 
of better moisture currently in GOES WV imagery just NE of the 
Bahamas). Isolated strong gusts near wet microbursts will remain 
possible, but these should be very few and far between, with the 
poor shear limiting storm intensity and longevity.

Mid level flow becomes even weaker and more westerly or even WNW 
starting early next week, as the westerlies remain to our N and the 
mid level ridge off the Southeast coast flattens and expands 
westward over FL/AL/GA, helping to curb access to the Gulf and 
Atlantic moisture sources and driving our PW back down. This should 
result in below-climo coverage, with a focus on mountain convection 
shifting into the NW Piedmont. The westerlies associated with the 
Canadian gyre and flat longwave trough over the Midwest/Great Lakes 
is expected to dig gently across the Mid Atlantic region starting 
Wed and continuing through late week, which should help support 
greater and more organized convection, but likely still no higher 
than good chance for now. 


KEY MESSAGE 2... 

As the flattening mid level ridge steadily expands westward over the 
Southeast and Gulf states starting early next week, surface lee 
troughing will sharpen over the Piedmont, with a downturn in cloud 
cover leading to greater warming at the surface, while mid level 
lapse rates remain modest to low. Low level thicknesses are expected 
to rise to 5-15 m above normal starting Sun, when highs should reach 
90 or higher most places. The hottest days of this stretch are 
expected to be Tue/Wed, when highs will be in the low-mid 90s, with 
lows in the low-mid 70s. The NWS experimental Heat Risk does reach 
the Major category in some areas then, suggesting a higher chance of 
heat-related illnesses for those without adequate cooling. By late 
next week, as the northern stream dips into the Mid Atlantic with an 
associated cold front approaching from the NW and N, the 
acceleration of broad cyclonic flow overhead and resulting uptick in 
clouds and pop coverage should help nudge highs down a bit by Fri.
